```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
```

```{r config}
source(here::here("R", "0_setup.R"))
source(here::here("R", "compile_functions.R"))
source(here::here("R", "plot_helpers.R"))

stock <- cfg$STOCK_SLUG %||% cfg$SPECIES_SLUG
sp <- tolower(cfg$SPECIES_NAME)
Sp <- cfg$SPECIES_NAME
area_label <- if (length(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS)) {
  paste("ICES subareas", paste(unlist(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS), collapse = " and "))
} else cfg$REGION
area_short <- if (length(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS)) {
  paste0("ICES ", paste(unlist(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS), collapse = "–"))
} else cfg$REGION
inside_label <- paste("Inside", area_short)
compiled_path <- file.path(out_dir, "compiled-data.rds")
metadata_path <- file.path(out_dir, "compile-metadata.rds")
# Last complete year: LAST_YEAR in config.yaml, or the year before the current year,
# because the current year's surveys are not yet complete. Numeric literal for DuckDB.
last_year <- as.integer(cfg$LAST_YEAR %||% (as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - 1L))
```

# Purpose

This document selects the IMR bottom-trawl survey data used for the `r sp` (*`r cfg$SPECIES_LATIN`*) survey indices in `r area_label` (stock `r cfg$STOCK_CODE`). `r cfg$PURPOSE`

The document answers which surveys, hauls and catch records enter the indices, and which are excluded and why. Its output is the compiled station dataset in `data/output/`, which is described further in the companion data report ([`r stock`-3-data](`r stock`-3-data.html)) and is the input to the spatiotemporal sdmTMB models [@Vihtakari2026]. Species, survey and model settings are read at run time from `config.yaml`.

```{r compile, eval=params$recompile}
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(
  path.expand(Sys.getenv("BES_DATABASE_PATH",
                         "~/IMR_biotic_BES_database/bioticexplorer.duckdb")),
  read_only = TRUE
))
db_meta <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM metadata")

res <- compile_species_stations(con, cfg, last_year)
dt <- add_response_and_covariates(res$stations, cfg) |>
  clean_tow_speed(cfg$TOW_SPEED_LIMITS %||% c(1.5, 6))
# Hauls positioned in deep water while the recorded depth is shallow have a wrong position.
position_errors <- flag_position_errors(dt, cfg$POSITION_ERROR_DEPTH %||% 1500,
                                        cfg$POSITION_ERROR_RATIO %||% 3)
dt <- dplyr::filter(dt, !haul_id %in% position_errors$haul_id)

lengths <- collect_lengths(con, cfg, dt)
length_limits <- unlist(cfg$LENGTH_LIMITS %||% c(5, 200)) # plausible lengths (cm)
length_outliers <- dplyr::filter(lengths, length_cm < length_limits[1] |
                                   length_cm > length_limits[2])
lengths <- dplyr::filter(lengths, length_cm >= length_limits[1],
                         length_cm <= length_limits[2])
lw <- fit_length_weight(lengths, cfg$LW_OUTLIER_SD %||% 4)
dt <- add_fishable_biomass(dt, lengths, lw, cfg$OVER_CM)

positive_observations <- collect_positive_observations(con, cfg, last_year)
distance_check <- distance_diagnostics(con, cfg, last_year)
quality_codes <- quality_code_table(con)
other_data <- other_data_summary(con, cfg)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

dir.create(here::here("ai", "review"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_csv(position_errors,
                 here::here("ai", "review", paste0(stock, "-position-errors.csv")))
readr::write_csv(res$diagnostics$duplicates,
                 here::here("ai", "review", paste0(stock, "-duplicate-hauls.csv")))
readr::write_csv(res$diagnostics$incomplete,
                 here::here("ai", "review", paste0(stock, "-incomplete-catches.csv")))

compile_metadata <- list(
  data_downloaded_at_label = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"),
  db_updated = format(as.POSIXct(db_meta$timeend[1]), "%Y-%m-%d"),
  diagnostics = res$diagnostics[c("n_candidate_rows", "n_valid_hauls",
                                  "n_qualifying_missions")],
  n_duplicates = nrow(res$diagnostics$duplicates),
  n_incomplete = nrow(res$diagnostics$incomplete),
  incomplete_by_series = res$diagnostics$incomplete,
  n_multi_sample = nrow(res$diagnostics$multi_sample),
  lw = lw[c("a", "b", "n")],
  lw_plot = lw$plot,
  lw_outlier_sd = cfg$LW_OUTLIER_SD %||% 4,
  n_lw_outliers = nrow(lw$outliers),
  position_errors = dplyr::select(position_errors, haul_id, year, cruiseseries, platformname,
                                  longitudestart, latitudestart, depth_recorded, depth_gebco,
                                  biomass, count),
  n_speed_flag = sum(dt$speed_flag),
  tow_speed_limits = unlist(cfg$TOW_SPEED_LIMITS %||% c(1.5, 6)),
  length_limits = length_limits,
  n_length_outliers = nrow(length_outliers),
  positive_observations = positive_observations,
  distance_check = distance_check,
  quality_codes = quality_codes,
  other_data = other_data
)
saveRDS(dt, compiled_path)
saveRDS(lengths, file.path(out_dir, "length-data.rds"))
saveRDS(compile_metadata, metadata_path)
```

```{r load}
dt <- readRDS(compiled_path)
compile_metadata <- readRDS(metadata_path)
dt$cruiseseries <- order_cruise_series(dt$cruiseseries, dt$year)
cs_cols <- cruise_series_colours(levels(dt$cruiseseries))
n_fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = " ")
included_surveys <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$missionid)
latest <- dplyr::slice_max(dt, start_time, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

# Data

The station and catch data were read from a local copy of the IMR Biotic database compiled with [BioticExplorerServer](https://github.com/DeepWaterIMR/BioticExplorerServer) [@BioticExplorerServer], last updated on `r compile_metadata$db_updated`, and extracted on `r compile_metadata$data_downloaded_at_label`.

## Stock area

The stock is defined by `r area_label`. The overview map shows all quality-filtered research bottom-trawl hauls with `r sp` in the Northeast Atlantic, coloured by whether the haul lies inside the stock area (@fig-stock-area). Hauls outside the stock area belong to neighbouring stocks and are not used. Of the `r n_fmt(nrow(compile_metadata$positive_observations))` positive hauls on the map, `r n_fmt(sum(compile_metadata$positive_observations$inside))` lie inside `r area_label`.

```{r stock-area-map}
stock_area <- read_stock_area(cfg)
obs <- compile_metadata$positive_observations |>
  dplyr::mutate(Location = factor(dplyr::if_else(inside, inside_label, "Outside"),
                                  levels = c("Outside", inside_label))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Location)
lim <- unlist(cfg$MAP_LIMITS)

base_area <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(limits = lim, bathymetry = TRUE, bathy.style = "rcb",
                                  bathy.alpha = 0.35, land.col = "grey85",
                                  land.border.col = "grey60", legends = FALSE,
                                  base_size = 9, rotate = TRUE)
area_map_height <- map_fig_height(base_area, extra = 0.7) # before geom_sf() resets limits
p_area <- base_area +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = stock_area, fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.15, colour = "#0072B2",
                   linewidth = 0.6) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(
    data = obs, ggplot2::aes(longitudestart, latitudestart, fill = Location),
    shape = 21, size = 1, stroke = 0.15, colour = "black", crs = 4326
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = stats::setNames(c("#56B4E9", "#E69F00"),
                                                     c("Outside", inside_label)),
                             name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r, fig.height = area_map_height}
#| label: fig-stock-area
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0(area_label, " (blue) and quality-filtered research bottom-trawl hauls with ", sp, " in the Northeast Atlantic, ", cfg$FIRST_YEAR, "–", max(dt$year), ". Orange: inside the stock area; light blue: outside. Hauls without ", sp, " are not shown.")'
ggOceanMaps::reorder_layers(p_area)
```

## Haul filter {#sec-haul-filter}

A haul was retained when it met all criteria in @tbl-filter-criteria. The rules follow index-wise `data-filtering.md`; the meaning of each retained quality code is taken from the reference tables of the Biotic database [see also the BAIT quality-code documentation].

```{r}
#| label: tbl-filter-criteria
tibble::tribble(
  ~Field, ~`Retained values`, ~Meaning,
  "gearcategory", "Bottom trawls", "Bottom-trawl gear only",
  "missiontypename", "Forskningsfartøy, Leiefartøy", "Research vessels and chartered vessels; reference fleet, commercial sampling and coast guard excluded",
  "startyear", paste0(cfg$FIRST_YEAR, "–", last_year), "Years included; the current year is excluded until its surveys are complete (LAST_YEAR)",
  "Stock area", if (length(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS)) paste0("icesarea ", paste0("27.", unlist(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS), ".*", collapse = ", ")) else "inside REGION_FILE polygon", area_label,
  "gearcondition", "1, 2", "1: gear OK; 2: minor damage with no material effect on catch",
  "samplequality", "1 (CoastalS: 1, 2)", "1: preselected position, trawl sensors normal; 2: deployed on an acoustic registration or other fish information, sensors normal",
  "stationtype", "missing, 1, 3, 9, 13", "Missing: ordinary unflagged station; 1: part of a 24-hour station; 3: gear trial that is also a regular fish station; 9: regular fish station; 13: additional preselected station",
  "distance", "0.3–5 nmi", "Towed distance usable for swept area",
  "gear", "not 3100, 3101, 3130", "Unspecified bottom-trawl codes removed"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Haul filter criteria. Hauls meeting all criteria were retained.")
```

The filter was applied in the database before the records were collected; the sample-quality rule, which depends on the cruise series, was applied immediately after collection (@lst-filter-expression).

```{r}
#| lst-label: lst-filter-expression
#| lst-cap: "Haul filter applied to the Biotic `stnall` table (from `standard_haul_filter()`, `apply_samplequality()` and `in_stock_area()` in `R/compile_functions.R`)."
#| code-fold: false
#| eval: false
stnall |>
  dplyr::filter(
    gearcategory == "Bottom trawls",
    missiontypename %in% c("Forskningsfartøy", "Leiefartøy"),
    startyear >= cfg$FIRST_YEAR,
    startyear <= last_year,
    !is.na(distance), !is.na(latitudestart), !is.na(longitudestart),
    latitudestart > 0,
    gearcondition %in% c("1", "2"),
    is.na(stationtype) | stationtype %in% c("1", "3", "9", "13"),
    distance >= 0.3, distance <= 5,
    is.na(gear) | !gear %in% c("3100", "3101", "3130")
  ) |>
  area_filter_lazy(cfg) |>   # ICES-area code (STOCK_SUBAREAS) or polygon bounding box
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::filter(in_stock_area(dplyr::pick(dplyr::everything()), cfg)) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(cruiseseriescode) & cruiseseriescode == "23",
      samplequality %in% c("1", "2"),
      samplequality %in% "1"
    )
  )
```

The coastal survey (CoastalS, cruise-series code 23) accepts sample-quality codes 1 and 2, whereas other cruise series require code 1. In its early years the coastal survey targeted saithe acoustically. We assume that `r sp` was nevertheless sampled at random with respect to those registrations, so code 2 hauls are kept for CoastalS.

Missing station types are retained explicitly, because most ordinary stations carry no station type and a database `IN` test would otherwise drop them. Russian data are `r if (isTRUE(cfg$INCLUDE_RUSSIAN)) "included" else "excluded"` (`INCLUDE_RUSSIAN` in `config.yaml`); `r n_fmt(sum(dt$nation %in% c("140", "90")))` retained hauls are Russian.

The filter gave `r n_fmt(compile_metadata$diagnostics$n_valid_hauls)` valid hauls in `r area_label`. Hauls where the length sample exceeded the catch (`r compile_metadata$n_duplicates` hauls) and hauls where `r sp` was recorded without a catch weight (`r compile_metadata$n_incomplete` hauls) were removed; their identifiers are listed in `ai/review/`. In `r compile_metadata$n_multi_sample` hauls, `r sp` was recorded in more than one catch sample; these samples were treated as additive and summed.


### Tow distance and unspecified gear

The tow-distance limits (0.3–5 nmi) are the generic index-wise rule developed for other species. To check them for `r sp`, @fig-tow-distance shows the distribution of tow distance for all hauls that passed the other haul criteria and for hauls with `r sp`. `r dc <- compile_metadata$distance_check; pos <- dplyr::filter(dc, catch_kg > 0); paste0("Of the ", n_fmt(nrow(pos)), " hauls with ", sp, ", ", sum(pos$distance < 0.3, na.rm = TRUE), " were shorter than 0.3 nmi, ", sum(pos$distance > 5, na.rm = TRUE), " longer than 5 nmi and ", sum(is.na(pos$distance)), " lacked a distance, so the limits keep ", round(100 * mean(pos$distance >= 0.3 & pos$distance <= 5, na.rm = TRUE), 1), " % of them")`. Catch per nautical mile decreased with tow distance (@tbl-tow-distance), so catches did not scale proportionally with tow length; the shortest tows gave the highest catch rates and are the most sensitive to errors in recorded distance. <!-- State the decision: keep the generic limits or adapt them for the species, with the reason. -->

```{r}
#| label: fig-tow-distance
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Tow distance of all hauls passing the other haul criteria and of hauls with ", sp, " (logarithmic scale). Dashed lines: the 0.3 and 5 nmi limits.")'
dc <- compile_metadata$distance_check |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(distance), distance > 0)
dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(dc, group = "All hauls"),
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::filter(dc, catch_kg > 0), group = paste("Hauls with", sp))
) |>
  ggplot(aes(distance)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#0072B2", colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.3, 5), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~group, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Tow distance (nmi)", y = "Hauls")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tow-distance
dc |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Distance (nmi)` = cut(distance, c(0, 0.3, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, Inf))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(`Distance (nmi)`) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Hauls = dplyr::n(), `Positive hauls` = sum(catch_kg > 0),
                   `Median catch (kg)` = round(stats::median(catch_kg[catch_kg > 0]), 1),
                   `Median catch per nmi (kg)` = round(stats::median(catch_kg[catch_kg > 0] /
                                                                    distance[catch_kg > 0]), 1),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Hauls and ", sp, " catches by tow distance, before the distance filter. Medians are for hauls with ", sp, "."))
```

The unspecified bottom-trawl codes (3100, 3101, 3130) occurred in `r sum(compile_metadata$distance_check$gear %in% c("3100", "3101", "3130"))` hauls, of which `r sum(compile_metadata$distance_check$gear %in% c("3100", "3101", "3130") & compile_metadata$distance_check$catch_kg > 0)` caught `r sp`. Removing them has a negligible effect on the data.

## Surveys and cruise series

A survey means one cruise. A survey was included when at least one positive `r sp` catch passed the haul filter inside `r area_label` (the encountered-on-a-cruise rule). All valid hauls of an included survey were retained, so hauls without `r sp` in those surveys are true zeros. Other surveys in the same cruise series were not included unless they also caught `r sp`. Included surveys were afterwards grouped by cruise series; surveys without a cruise-series code were grouped as `Other` only after they qualified.

The rule selected `r included_surveys` surveys and `r n_fmt(nrow(dt))` hauls (@tbl-survey-selection). `r cs_top <- dt |> dplyr::count(cruiseseries, wt = biomass > 0, sort = TRUE); paste0(cs_top$cruiseseries[1], " and ", cs_top$cruiseseries[2])` contributed most positive hauls (`r round(100 * sum(cs_top$n[1:2]) / sum(cs_top$n))` %).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-survey-selection
dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(`Cruise series` = cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Code = {codes <- unique(stats::na.omit(dplyr::na_if(cruiseseriescode, "NA")))
            paste(codes[order(as.numeric(sub(",.*", "", codes)))], collapse = ", ")},
    Surveys = dplyr::n_distinct(missionid),
    `First year` = min(year), `Last year` = max(year),
    Months = format_months(month),
    Hauls = dplyr::n(),
    `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0),
    `Catch (kg)` = round(sum(biomass)),
    `Zero fraction (%)` = round(100 * mean(biomass == 0), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Cruise series of the included surveys with ", sp,
                                " in ", area_label, ". Zero fraction is the percentage of retained hauls without ", sp, "."))
```

Surveys grouped as `Other` either have no cruise-series code or belong to cruise series with few surveys in the stock area. They are listed one by one in @tbl-other-surveys, with the short name of the cruise series where a code exists, so that each survey can be judged separately.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-other-surveys
dt |>
  dplyr::filter(cruiseseries == "Other") |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year = year, Vessel = platformname, Cruise = cruise,
                  Series = survey_label(cruiseseriescode, series_short, cruise, cfg)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Months = format_months(month),
                   Gear = paste(sort(unique(geartype)), collapse = ", "),
                   Hauls = dplyr::n(), `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Included surveys grouped as Other. Series gives the short name and code of the cruise series, or the survey name from SURVEY_NAMES in config.yaml for surveys without a code; – means neither is known.")
```

## Dataset overview

@tbl-data-overview summarises the compiled dataset.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-overview
tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c("Database last updated", "Data extracted", "Latest haul",
             "Retained hauls", paste0("Hauls with ", sp), "True-zero hauls (zero fraction)",
             "Included surveys", "Cruise series", "Years", "Number of years",
             "Removed: length sample exceeds catch", "Removed: catch weight missing"),
  Value = c(compile_metadata$db_updated, compile_metadata$data_downloaded_at_label,
            paste0(format(latest$station_date), " (", latest$cruiseseries, ")"),
            n_fmt(nrow(dt)), n_fmt(sum(dt$biomass > 0)),
            paste0(n_fmt(sum(dt$biomass == 0)), " (", sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(dt$biomass == 0)), " %)"),
            included_surveys, dplyr::n_distinct(dt$cruiseseries),
            paste0(min(dt$year), "–", max(dt$year)), dplyr::n_distinct(dt$year),
            compile_metadata$n_duplicates, compile_metadata$n_incomplete)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Overview of the compiled ", sp, " dataset."))
```

# Analysis

## Survey catch and effort

Catch is the total recorded `r sp` biomass per haul, and occurrence is the number of positive hauls. The cruise series differ in both, and they do not rank identically by catch and by positive hauls (@fig-survey-catch-overview). Split by year, the same quantities show when each series entered the time series and how uneven the annual coverage is (@fig-survey-catch-year).

```{r}
#| label: fig-survey-catch-overview
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Total ", sp, " catch (t) and number of positive hauls by cruise series. The panels use independent y-axis scales.")'
dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(`Total catch (t)` = sum(biomass) / 1000,
                   `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-cruiseseries) |>
  ggplot(aes(cruiseseries, value, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-survey-catch-year
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual number of positive ", sp, " hauls (A) and total catch (B) by cruise series.")'
annual <- dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(year, cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(positive = sum(biomass > 0), catch_t = sum(biomass) / 1000,
                   .groups = "drop")
p1 <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, positive, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2030, 5), expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Positive hauls", fill = "Cruise series") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
p2 <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, catch_t, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2030, 5), expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Catch (t)", fill = "Cruise series") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
cowplot::plot_grid(p1, p2, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", rel_heights = c(4, 5.2))
```

## Survey positions

The cruise series cover overlapping but different parts of the stock area, and positive hauls are a spatially clustered subset of the effort in every series (@fig-survey-positions).

```{r survey-positions-map}
n_series <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$cruiseseries)
p_pos <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = dt, legends = FALSE, base_size = 8, rotate = TRUE,
                              expand.factor = 1, land.col = "grey85",
                              land.border.col = "grey60") +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = dplyr::filter(dt, biomass == 0),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart), colour = "grey40", size = 0.15, alpha = 0.5,
    crs = 4326) +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = dplyr::filter(dt, biomass > 0),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart), colour = "#D55E00", size = 0.5, crs = 4326) +
  facet_wrap(~cruiseseries, ncol = 3) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank())
positions_map_height <- map_fig_height(p_pos, ncol = 3, nrow = ceiling(n_series / 3),
                                       extra = 0.3 * ceiling(n_series / 3), side = 0.3)
```

```{r, fig.height = positions_map_height}
#| label: fig-survey-positions
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Retained hauls by cruise series. Grey: hauls without ", sp, " (true zeros); orange: hauls with ", sp, ".")'
p_pos
```

## Gear

All catches were converted to density using a common `r cfg$GEAR_WIDTH` m effective width, and gear type is kept as a fixed effect in the models so that systematic gear differences can be estimated. `r gt <- dplyr::count(dt, geartype, sort = TRUE); paste0(gt$geartype[1], " trawls")` account for `r round(100 * gt$n[1] / sum(gt$n))` % of the hauls (@fig-gear-overview). Depth, tow distance and haul duration differ between cruise series and gears (@tbl-gear).

```{r}
#| label: fig-gear-overview
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Gear used in the included surveys. A: ", sp, " catch per positive haul by gear (number of hauls in brackets), coloured by cruise series, logarithmic scale. B: number of hauls by year and gear type.")'
gear_n <- dplyr::count(dt, gearname, name = "n_hauls")
gd <- dt |>
  dplyr::filter(biomass > 0) |>
  dplyr::left_join(gear_n, by = "gearname") |>
  dplyr::mutate(gear_label = paste0(gearname, " (", n_hauls, ")"))
p_gear <- ggplot(gd, aes(stats::reorder(gear_label, biomass, FUN = median), biomass,
                         fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, outlier.alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Catch per positive haul (kg)", fill = "Cruise series") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "right")
p_year <- dt |>
  dplyr::count(year, geartype) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, n, fill = geartype)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gear_colours()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2030, 5), expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Hauls", fill = "Gear type")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_gear, p_year, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", rel_heights = c(6, 4),
                   align = "v", axis = "lr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-gear
fmt_range <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return("–")
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f [%.", digits, "f–%.", digits, "f]"), mean(x), min(x), max(x))
}
dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(`Cruise series` = cruiseseries, `Gear type` = geartype, Gear = gearname) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Hauls = dplyr::n(), `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0),
                   `Depth (m)` = fmt_range(depth, 0),
                   `Distance (nmi)` = fmt_range(distance, 2),
                   `Duration (min)` = fmt_range(duration_min, 0),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Gear and haul characteristics by cruise series. Values are mean [minimum–maximum].")
```

## Survey timing

```{r timing-height}
timing_height <- round(0.2 * dplyr::n_distinct(dt$year) + 1.2, 1)
```

The cruise series occupy characteristic and largely stable parts of the year, so season is partly confounded with cruise series (@fig-survey-timing). Month is therefore included as a smooth term in the models, and the survey effect is examined in the model fits.

```{r, fig.height = timing_height}
#| label: fig-survey-timing
#| fig-cap: "Timing of the included surveys, newest year at the top. Segments span the first to last retained haul of each survey; cruise series are offset slightly within a year."
plot_survey_timing(dt, cs_cols)
```

## Gross-error screening

Recorded depths, positions, tow durations and length and weight records were screened for gross errors (@tbl-screening). Hauls positioned deeper than `r cfg$POSITION_ERROR_DEPTH %||% 1500` m on GEBCO while their recorded bottom depth is shallower than the GEBCO depth divided by `r cfg$POSITION_ERROR_RATIO %||% 3`, or missing, cannot have fished where they are positioned; the trawls were bottom trawls, and neither species lives pelagically. These hauls are removed, because their position is wrong (`r nrow(compile_metadata$position_errors)` hauls, `r sum(compile_metadata$position_errors$biomass > 0)` with `r sp`; listed in `ai/review/`). The towed distance is taken as correct, because it defines the swept area: where distance and duration imply a speed outside `r paste(compile_metadata$tow_speed_limits, collapse = '–')` knots, the duration is set to missing and the haul is kept. The length–weight outliers are individual weights that deviate strongly from the log-length–log-weight regression; they are left out of that regression, which predicts the weight of each measured fish for the fishable share, but the fish stay in the length data. Depth mismatches are reported but not removed, because the recorded depth is the better measure on steep slopes; they are examined in the data report.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-screening
tibble::tibble(
  Check = c("Depth missing or non-positive; filled from GEBCO",
            "Recorded depth differs from GEBCO by more than a factor of 2",
            "Haul on land according to GEBCO (depth ≤ 0)",
            paste0("Length records outside ", compile_metadata$length_limits[1], "–",
                   compile_metadata$length_limits[2], " cm (removed)"),
            paste0("Hauls with a wrong position (GEBCO depth > ", cfg$POSITION_ERROR_DEPTH %||% 1500, " m, recorded depth < GEBCO / ", cfg$POSITION_ERROR_RATIO %||% 3, " or missing; removed)"),
            paste0("Tow speed (distance / duration) outside ", paste(compile_metadata$tow_speed_limits, collapse = "–"), " knots (duration set to missing; haul kept)"),
            paste0("Individual weights with |standardised residual| > ", compile_metadata$lw_outlier_sd %||% 4, " in the log-length–log-weight regression (left out of the length–weight regression used to predict weight at length; fish kept in the length data)"),
            "Positive hauls without length measurements"),
  Count = c(sum(dt$depth_source == "GEBCO"),
            sum(dt$depth_ratio > 2 | dt$depth_ratio < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(dt$depth_gebco <= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            compile_metadata$n_length_outliers,
            nrow(compile_metadata$position_errors),
            compile_metadata$n_speed_flag,
            compile_metadata$n_lw_outliers,
            sum(dt$biomass > 0 & dt$n_measured == 0))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Gross-error screening of the compiled ", sp, " data."))
```

## Other data in the database

The database also holds `r sp` records that are not research bottom-trawl hauls, such as reference-fleet, commercial and coast-guard samples (@tbl-other-data). These are not survey hauls with a known swept area and are not used for the trawl index. <!-- State here any other use of these data in the project, e.g. setting a fishable-length threshold. -->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-other-data
compile_metadata$other_data |>
  dplyr::rename(`Mission type` = missiontypename, `Gear category` = gearcategory,
                Stations = stations, `First year` = first_year, `Last year` = last_year) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("All IMR Biotic stations with ", sp, " in ", area_label, " by mission type and gear category, before filtering."))
```

# Results and recommendations

The compiled station dataset is written to `data/output/`, which is git-ignored.

**Ready for downstream use.** The dataset contains `r n_fmt(nrow(dt))` bottom-trawl hauls from `r included_surveys` surveys in `r min(dt$year)`–`r max(dt$year)`, of which `r n_fmt(sum(dt$biomass > 0))` caught `r sp` (@tbl-data-overview). Its zeros are true absences within surveys that caught `r sp`. Gear type, depth, month and cruise series are available for every haul.

**Provisional.** The common `r cfg$GEAR_WIDTH` m effective width pushes gear differences into the gear fixed effect; if that effect cannot be estimated, the width assumption is the first to revisit. Keeping sample-quality code 2 for CoastalS assumes that `r sp` was sampled at random within those acoustically targeted hauls. The current year is excluded until its surveys are complete (`LAST_YEAR` in `config.yaml`).

**To decide in the data report and model fits.** Which cruise series and gear types to keep, and whether the irregular `Other` surveys add information or noise.
